mustFix.title: Fixture-local label hashes do not satisfy the live identity fields they occupy
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The corpus deliberately derives the universe key, snapshot id, and subject-scope commitment as bare SHA-256 hashes of opensip.fixture.g23.* labels, calls them FIXTURE-LOCAL rather than live Run identity, and copies those values into the asserted FactCandidateV1 and CoverageV1 objects.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: delivery.v2 defines TypeScriptSemanticUniverseKey as a Sha256Text produced from the domain-separated CVE1 encoding of TypeScriptSemanticUniverseV1, requires every CoverageKeyV1 sourceUniverseId to be that exact OpenUniverse key, requires subjectScopeCommitment to be the Sha256Text commitment over the exact sealed snapshot subject set, and requires candidate identity/context fields to equal admitted host context. Sha256Text matches ^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$, while every copied value is bare 64-hex. The stated label-hash constructions are also not the pinned constructions. An explicit NOT-LIVE disclaimer cannot make values valid in fields whose closed contract requires live contextual equality.
mustFix.counterexample: A host can reject every authored member for malformed or context-mismatched universe/scope/snapshot identity before reaching the provider-minted relation schema, Coverage-domain comparison, or unknown-to-covered check. Such a run would observe refusal while measuring none of EV-1, EV-2, or EV-3.
mustFix.impact: The three fixture files are not hostile-but-well-formed instances of the admitted types and cannot close OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING.
mustFix.requiredRepair: Author and digest-pin the exact already-defined host request/session context needed by the fixtures, then copy its correctly typed universe, snapshot, subject-scope, provider-build, stage, and anchor values into the payloads. Preserve the design-only and not-live-Run authority boundary, but do not use arbitrary label hashes as substitutes for closed payload values. Recompute every dependent byte and digest.

mustFix.title: The NT-3 JSON puts a hexadecimal text transcription in a FactCandidateV1 byte-string field
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The authored candidate contains canonicalRelationPayload: "a0" and justifies it as the lowercase-hex transcription quoted from fact-plane.v1 admittedRecordSchema.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: delivery.v2 FactCandidateV1 requires canonicalRelationPayload to be a deterministic-CBOR byte string. The pinned fact-plane.v1 transportRepresentation is more explicit: JSON vectors transcribe those bytes as canonicalRelationPayloadHex, and that transcription is not an additional wire field. Its admittedRecordSchema lowercase-hex field is the post-admission FactRecord representation, not the provider transport value. The subject instead places JSON text under the byte-string wire-field name in a candidate that is supposed to fail admission.
mustFix.counterexample: A closed-type decoder rejects the JSON string as the wrong wire value type without consulting the host-owned relation payload registry. That is a type-level failure, not NT-3 content-level relation-registry refusal of a well-formed FactCandidateV1.
mustFix.impact: EV-1 can pass for the wrong reason and cannot prove that the value was refused by the intended host relation-registry limb.
mustFix.requiredRepair: Use the pinned JSON-vector transcription boundary or actual wire bytes so the harness presents a byte string to FactCandidateV1 validation. Keep the intended provider-minted schema id or mismatched decoded payload as the content-level mutation, without importing the admitted FactRecord representation or inventing another field/schema.

mustFix.title: The Coverage cases use impossible TypeScript-provider relations and the widening entries are noncanonical
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The narrows/widens baseline contains declares/syntactic plus file/enumerated, and the widening payload adds package/manifest-declared on the theory that any live fact-plane relationRegistry key is usable. Its entry order is declares, file, package.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: delivery.v2 coverageDomain.relationResolutionById for typescript-semantic contains exactly declares, imports, references, calls, types, and reachability. StageRequestV1 relations outside that selected provider map are denied before provider execution; file and package belong to syntax-all, not typescript-semantic. Independently, full CoverageKeyV1 values must be sorted by ascending deterministic-CBOR bytes and CoverageV1 entries must follow that order. With the fixture's equal non-relation fields, the measured order is file/enumerated, package/manifest-declared, declares/syntactic, not the authored order.
mustFix.counterexample: The alleged host baseline containing file cannot be constructed for a TypeScript semantic-provider stage. If the widening payload is nevertheless injected, the host can reject an unsupported relation or unordered array before testing the single intended unrequested-key widening.
mustFix.impact: Neither EV-2 narrows nor EV-2 widens is an isolated, executable mutation relative to a legal D-002 TypeScript-provider request.
mustFix.requiredRepair: Build the baseline exclusively from the pinned typescript-semantic relation/rung map, use a different supported but unrequested full key for widening, sort all full keys by their deterministic-CBOR bytes, align entryOrdinal values, and recompute dependent commitments and fixture digests.

mustFix.title: Both Coverage commitments are compact-JSON hashes, not valid CoverageV1 commitments
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The two files carry bare values 6ce54577... and 47d44a07..., while the catalog says coverageCommitment is not live CVE1/deterministic-CBOR verification.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: delivery.v2 requires CoverageV1.coverageCommitment to be Sha256Text over deterministic-CBOR(entries). The authored values exactly reproduce SHA-256 over newline-free jq -c JSON for their current entries. A direct deterministic-CBOR re-encoding of those same current entries yields 21d7f24e389d1d8ccb7eae41c0e9fb4e72c7a693c2a581e7c03ca9b7db8cd635 and 92a165cd9943b6ff7ee508fa103016b4ce1802731375b9c706318f6bcfe504b6, respectively. The authored values also omit the required sha256: prefix. Correcting the other malformed fields will change the deterministic-CBOR preimages again.
mustFix.counterexample: A host that validates the frame commitment rejects both files before domain conformance. The shared first file then makes both narrows and unknown-to-covered pass by commitment failure, while the widening file does the same independently.
mustFix.impact: All three NT-5 catalog members are incapable of isolating their claimed mutation and the corpus's statement that they are closed CoverageV1 payloads is false.
mustFix.requiredRepair: After repairing the exact closed entries and their canonical order, compute Sha256Text from the pinned deterministic-CBOR entries bytes, include the required prefix, and independently reproduce each result before freezing successor fixture digests.

mustFix.title: The catalog invents an abbreviated Coverage-baseline vocabulary and does not retain an exact unknown baseline
mustFix.subjectEvidence: The catalog represents domains as strings such as declares/syntactic and represents the EV-3 baseline as the new string declares/syntactic recorded unknown. It reuses the narrows payload file for EV-3 and asserts that these catalog strings are distinct host-requested baselines.
mustFix.refutingMeasurement: RequestedCoverageDomainV1 is a closed object containing SubjectScopeV1, sorted full CoverageKeyV1 values, and domainCommitment. A full key has eight fields; relation/resolution shorthand is not that type and cannot prove equality, ordering, or commitment. Coverage state is not a requested-domain key field: unknown belongs to CoverageResultV1 and requires a live deficiency. The EV-3 string pins neither an exact prior/host-owned CoverageResultV1 nor a deficiency, and the EV-2 strings pin no exact host request bytes. Thus the strings coin an ungoverned encoding vocabulary while failing the occupancy's requirement to retain the host-requested domain and the baseline with unknown.
mustFix.counterexample: Two legal full domains can share the same declares/syntactic shorthand while differing in universe, target, scope, producer version, or schema version. Likewise, multiple materially different unknown results collapse to declares/syntactic recorded unknown. A harness cannot reconstruct which exact baseline the digest-pinned shared payload is supposed to mutate.
mustFix.impact: The nominally different prose string does not supply the distinct exact host baseline required for unknown-to-covered, and no NT-5 member is a self-contained exact-byte record. OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING remains open.
mustFix.requiredRepair: Pin an exact closed RequestedCoverageDomainV1 for each EV-2 case and an exact already-authorized host state/record that carries EV-3 unknown, including its live deficiency, or leave that representation as explicit leftover design until its owner defines it. Do not substitute slash strings or add fields to CoverageV1. Keep shared payload bytes only if the separately pinned exact contexts make the two cases unambiguous.

summary: REJECT at 5 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Custody, lineage, authority, live required-now 28, and all cited hashes pass, but the authored bytes do not implement the four named hostile-but-well-formed initial states. Arbitrary bare label hashes occupy fields that require exact typed live context; the NT-3 JSON puts hex text in a byte-string transport field; the NT-5 baselines use file/package relations unavailable to the TypeScript semantic provider and the widening array is noncanonical; both Coverage commitments hash compact JSON instead of deterministic CBOR and omit the Sha256Text prefix; and the slash-string baselines are neither closed RequestedCoverageDomainV1 bytes nor an exact unknown CoverageResult baseline. Each defect permits rejection before the behavior G23 is meant to measure, so OBL-G23-FX-AUTHORING remains open.
verdictRule: ACCEPT only at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Measured: 5 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX, so the verdict is REJECT.
